 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the order of dismissal dated 21.02.2013 passed by the Presiding Officer, Fast Track Court-III and Additional M.A.C.T. at Mysore ('the Tribunal' in short) in MVC No.1016/2010.
For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Briefly stated the facts are that, on 02.05.2010 at about 11:45 am, the father of the petitioners one Keshava Rao Chowhan, while walking on the road at Davani Beedi Circle of Hunsur, hit by a motor cycle bearing No.KA-45/K-1191 causing him head injury and injury to the other parts of the body.
The injured was taken to J.S.S. Hospital, Mysuru and thereafter he was admitted to Mission Keshava Rao Chowhan vs Swamy Gowda on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6770930/
2 Hospital and then at K.R. Hospital, Mysuru.

sentences.text: Thereafter, he was also taken treatment at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
Seeking compensation, the injured Keshava Rao Chowhan has filed the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act.
After filing of the petition on 23.05.2012, he was succumbed to death.
Hence, his legal representatives have filed the claim as dependants for award of compensation.
Claim is opposed by the respondents.

After taking the NC: 2023:KHC:20972 evidence, the Tribunal passed the impugned judgment dismissing the claim petition on the ground that there is a nexus between the accident and the death of the deceased.
Aggrieved by the same LRs of the deceased have filed this appeal on various grounds.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri. Mahadeva Swamy.

P, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri. S.
Srishaila, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and Sri. Prakasha.
H.C, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place on 02.05.2010, for the injuries treatment was provided by them throughout till his death on 23.05.2012.
This has been established by producing the medical evidence.
Therefore, compensation ought to have been awarded for the loss of dependency.
Learned counsel also argued that, even if that is not NC: 2023:KHC:20972 explained, the petitioners have spent huge money towards treatment and medical records are placed before the Tribunal.

The deceased was under hospitalization at Mission Hospital, Mysuru for a period of 33 days, 10 days at K.R.
Hospital, Mysuru and 5 days at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, in all 48 days, and after discharge, he was continuously on follow up treatment.
Money spent towards the treatment by the petitioners needs to be reimbursed.
The Tribunal has carried away the gap of two years from the date of accident and the date of death.

Hence, he sought for award of compensation accepting that the death of the deceased was on account of the accident and there is a nexus between the cause of death and the injuries sustained by the deceased Keshava Rao Chowhan in the accident in question.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the owner of the vehicle contended that the accident though took NC: 2023:KHC:20972 place on 02.05.2010, after the treatment,
the injured Keshava Rao Chowhan was healed up and for this reason he has filed the petition for compensation for the injuries.
If he was alive, he was entitled for compensation under the different heads including the medical expenses.
The death of the deceased was on 23.05.2012 i.e., after two years of the accident.
There is no evidence placed before the Tribunal that the deceased was died on account of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, the Tribunal is right in dismissing the claim that there is no nexus between the accident and the death and supported the impugned judgment.
7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that two years after the accident, the death was occurred.
The nature of injuries sustained by Keshava Rao Chowhan is not so serious which will affect on his life and there is no nexus between death and the accident.

The Tribunal has NC: 2023:KHC:20972 appreciated the material on record and the medical evidence did point out Keshava Rao Chowhan vs Swamy Gowda on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6770930/
3 that the deceased was suffering from varicose vein for his legs and he has taken treatment for it and also for his diabetes.

sentences.text: The cause of death is for some other reason and it is nothing to do with the injuries sustained by him in the accident.
Hence, he supported the impugned judgment.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties and perused the materials on record.

9. There is no dispute as to the accident in which the deceased Keshava Rao Chowhan has sustained injuries and he has taken treatment at Mission Hospital, Mysuru, K.R. Hospital, Mysuru and Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru and he was under hospitalization.

The medical records point out that the deceased was under hospitalization at Mission Hospital from 02.05.2010 to 03.06.2010, at K.R. NC:
2023:KHC:20972 Hospital from 03.06.2010 to 12.06.2010 and at Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru from 30.06.2011 to 04.07.2011.
In total he was under hospitalization for 48 days.
The last discharge of the injured was on 04.07.2011.

From 04.07.2011 to 23.05.2012, the petitioners are required to establish the deceased was under treatment for the injuries that he has sustained in the accident in question to connect the nexus to the death.

10. The petitioners have examined PW-4 Dr. Ramesh Mahadev Thambat, the Professor of Surgery,
Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru the Doctor who treated the injured Keshava Rao Chowhan.

He has pointed out that the injured Keshava Rao Chowhan was suffering from varicose vein, ulcer and cellulites and epilics for which he has been treated and these are the ailments which are nothing to do with the injuries that the deceased suffered in the accident.
The evidence on record did not point out that after NC: 2023:KHC:20972 the death of the deceased, he was subjected to post- mortem examination.
Police investigation points out that the driver of the vehicle has been charge sheeted in C.C. No.144/2010 for the offence under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.

Though there was an accident in which the deceased has suffered, the head injury which is described in Ex.P-7 wound certificate such as Hemorrhagic/contusion of left basal ganglia region, multiple pockets of air in subarchanoid spaces, fracture of right temporal bone.
These are the injuries that have been treated in the Hospital and the deceased was discharged and he was recovered and for this reason he has filed the claim for the injuries that he has sustained.
The treatment that has been given at the Victoria Hospital as deposed by the PW-4 is not for the accidental injuries and is a different ailment which has nothing to do with the accident.
I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.

The Tribunal has clearly recorded its finding that though the deceased Keshava Rao Chowhan, sustained injury in the accident in question and has taken treatment, but in death was on 23.05.2012 i.e., two years after the accident.
Hospitalization for treatment is total 43 days.

sentences.text: 4 condition of the petitioner, any follow-up treatment taken or not has not been explained before the Tribunal.
It is the duty of the petitioners to explain the cause of death, its nexus with the injury sustained in the accident.
In the absence of evidence it is very difficult to record a finding that the death of the deceased was on account of the accidental injuries only.
Hence, the Tribunal is right in holding that the nexus between the accident and the death has not been explained.
The material on record did point out that several records are placed before the Tribunal to explain that the injured has spent money towards his treatment.
In this regard, Ex.P-11 is the hospital bills of Mission Hospital, Mysuru and Ex.P-13 is the bills regarding money spent towards medicines.
There is no dispute as to the head injury sustained by the deceased and he being treated in the hospital.

The medical bills itself come to Rs.89,704/. Having regard to the deceased was under hospitalization for 44 days incidental expenses that has been spent by the family members could also considered at Rs.17,150/-.
If all these things are taken into consideration, the treatment expenses comes Rs.1,06,854/- rounded off to Rs.1,07,000/-.
This is what the petitioners being the children of the deceased are entitled.
If the deceased was not met with the accident, he could have saved this money as an estate to his children.
The Tribunal ought to have considered these aspects but dismissed the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:20972 claim petition and in the circumstances, it is erroneous.
The petitioners being the children of the deceased are entitled for the money spent towards the treatment to an extent of Rs.1,07,000/-.
Accordingly, the claim petition deserves to be allowed.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment is modified accordingly.

(iii) The appellants/petitioners would be entitled for compensation of Rs.1,07,000/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The first respondent/insurer is directed to satisfy the award within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
